answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Anchoring. Each identity must hit a narrow predicted band of behaviour (action counts, timing, counterparty mix) across consecutive epochs; deviation beyond a fixed ledge of tolerance flags the identity for review. The prediction derives from an orchard of prior per-identity traces, not shared templates. A fresh duplicate cannot fake continuity without replaying months of matched activity. Every new identity acts as a beacon for its lineage, so attackers pay the full cost of sustained, band-consistent operation per clone rather than a one-time registration.
